key_insight: Turbulence in a T-shaped mixer develops in two stages: a near-junction jet-like regime followed by a decay region with power-law losses, with velocity and scalar variance showing different scaling behavior.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict mixing performance and pressure/transport behavior in T-mixers used for chemical processing, especially when designing toward turbulent operation.
method: Direct numerical simulations of the turbulent T-mixer flow
Reynolds numbers up to Re = 2000 at Schmidt number Sc = 1
Streamwise analysis of turbulence, dissipation, scalar variance, and effective diffusion
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DNS across Re up to 2000, identifying jet-like self-similar behavior near the junction and power-law decay further downstream, with scalar profiles and effective diffusion quantified from time-averaged fields.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on Sc = 1 and a specific T-mixer geometry, so the observed scaling and mixing behavior may not transfer directly to fluids with different diffusivity or to other mixer designs.
paper_title: Stages of turbulence generation and decay in a T-shaped mixer
